code: read_all <- function(file) {   lapply(file.path(root, pkgs$path, file), function(f) {     if (file.exists(f)) toml_read(f) else list()   }) } info <- read_all("Package.toml") versions <- read_all("Versions.toml") deps <- read_all("Deps.toml") pkgs$repo <- vapply(info, `[[`, "", "repo") pkgs$subdir <- vapply(info, function(x) !is.null(x$subdir), NA) sort(table(sub("^https?://([^/]+)/.*$", "\\1", pkgs$repo)), decreasing = TRUE) #>  #>     github.com     gitlab.com   codeberg.org gitlab.gwdg.de      git.sr.ht  #>          14435             73              9              4              2  #> gitlab.emse.fr  #>              1 sum(pkgs$subdir) #> [1] 619 pkgs$n_versions <- lengths(versions) yanked <- function(v) sum(vapply(v, function(e) isTRUE(e$yanked), NA)) pkgs$n_yanked <- vapply(versions, yanked, 0L) head(pkgs[order(-pkgs$n_versions), c("name", "n_versions", "n_yanked")], 10) #>                  name n_versions n_yanked #> 2466       DiffEqBase        631        3 #> 666         SciMLBase        578        3 #> 8572  ModelingToolkit        550        1 #> 94       Reactant_jll        443        0 #> 13455          Meshes        428        0 #> 9030     Oceananigans        424        0 #> 1723   OrdinaryDiffEq        414        4 #> 9580            Trixi        353        0 #> 7303      LinearSolve        332        1 #> 7217           Enzyme        327        0 sum(pkgs$n_yanked) #> [1] 359

title: The Julia package registry
text: ask package depends now, take latest release keep Deps.toml sections whose range contains . range one version two joined -; short bound 1 stands every 1.x.y. Pre-releases (1.0.0-rc1) skipped build numbers (+0) ignored. depended-packages latest releases. Standard libraries LinearAlgebra registered, left :
code: version_parts <- function(v) {   as.integer(strsplit(sub("[-+].*$", "", v), ".", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]) }  latest <- function(v) {   v <- names(v)[!grepl("-", names(v))]   if (!length(v)) return(NA_character_)   v[order(numeric_version(sub("\\+.*$", "", v)), decreasing = TRUE)][1] }  # -1, 0 or 1 as version v is below, within or above a (possibly short) bound compare <- function(v, bound) {   b <- version_parts(bound)   d <- which(v[seq_along(b)] != b)   if (length(d)) sign(v[d[1]] - b[d[1]]) else 0 }  in_range <- function(v, range) {   bounds <- trimws(strsplit(range, "-", fixed = TRUE)[[1]])   lo <- bounds[1]   hi <- bounds[length(bounds)]   (lo == "*" || compare(v, lo) >= 0) && (hi == "*" || compare(v, hi) <= 0) }  deps_at <- function(d, v) {   if (is.na(v)) return(character())   v <- version_parts(v)   hit <- Filter(function(r) in_range(v, r), names(d))   sort(unique(as.character(unlist(lapply(d[hit], names))))) }  pkgs$latest <- vapply(versions, latest, "") pkgs$deps <- Map(deps_at, deps, pkgs$latest) pkgs$deps[[which(pkgs$name == "Xsum")]] #> [1] "xsum_jll" used <- table(unlist(pkgs$deps)) head(sort(used[names(used) %in% pkgs$name], decreasing = TRUE), 15) #>  #>          Statistics           Artifacts         JLLWrappers        StaticArrays  #>                2086                1910                1795                1373  #>       Distributions          DataFrames            Reexport           StatsBase  #>                1277                1272                1157                1155  #>     PrecompileTools                JSON DocStringExtensions    SpecialFunctions  #>                 822                 821                 791                 697  #>      DataStructures                 CSV       ProgressMeter  #>                 685                 680                 617

toml_read(file)[[1]]       if (is.null(names(artifact))) artifact[[1]] else artifact     }   ) } artifacts <- Map(first_artifact, jlls$name, tarballs) jlls$fortran <- vapply(artifacts, function(a) title: Usage guide
text: toml_parse() reads TOML text; toml_read() reads file, URL connection. return named list, keys order document gives .
code: doc <- ' title = "Example"  [server] host = "localhost" port = 8080 tags = ["web", "api"]  [[users]] name = "ana" admin = true  [[users]] name = "bo" ' x <- toml_parse(doc) str(x) #> List of 3 #>  $ title : chr "Example" #>  $ server:List of 3 #>   ..$ host: chr "localhost" #>   ..$ port: int 8080 #>   ..$ tags: chr [1:2] "web" "api" #>  $ users :List of 2 #>   ..$ :List of 2 #>   .. ..$ name : chr "ana" #>   .. ..$ admin: logi TRUE #>   ..$ :List of 1 #>   .. ..$ name: chr "bo" path <- tempfile(fileext = ".toml") writeLines(doc, path) toml_read(path)$server$port #> [1] 8080

what: Read only part of a document
title: Usage guide
text: select returns value path, written TOML key syntax: dots keys, quotes around keys need , [] array elements, counting 1. whole document still checked, since TOML lets table added anywhere , selected part becomes R values. path document error, never NULL:
code: toml_parse(doc, select = "server") #> $host #> [1] "localhost" #>  #> $port #> [1] 8080 #>  #> $tags #> [1] "web" "api" toml_parse(doc, select = "users[2].name") #> [1] "bo" toml_read(path, select = c("server", "tags")) #> [1] "web" "api" try(toml_parse(doc, select = "server.timeout")) #> Error : TOML document has no `server.timeout`: `server` has no `timeout`

title: Usage guide
text: Every TOML type maps one R type, chosen document’s syntax, never string looks like: datetimes = "keep" returns date-times RFC 3339 text, local_time = "difftime" returns times day seconds since midnight. big_integers decides happens past 2^53: toml_bigint (exact text, default), nearest double, error.

title: Usage guide
text: array whose elements share type becomes vector; integers floats together become double vector. Booleans never join numbers. Anything else list. one-element array marked () writing back gives array , e shows. simplify = "none" makes every array list.
code:
str(toml_parse("a = [1, 2]
b = [1, 2.5]
c = [true, 1]
d = []
e = [3]")) #> List of 5 #>  $ a: int [1:2] 1 2 #>  $ b: num [1:2] 1 2.5 #>  $ c:List of 2 #>   ..$ : logi TRUE #>   ..$ : int 1 #>  $ d: logi(0)  #>  $ e: 'AsIs' int 3

title: Usage guide
text: data_frame = TRUE turns array tables data frame: one row per table, columns first-seen key order, NA table lacks key.
code: toml_parse(doc, data_frame = TRUE)$users #>   name admin #> 1  ana  TRUE #> 2   bo    NA

title: Usage guide
text: toml_emit() writes named list TOML text; toml_write() writes file connection. table’s values come first, sub-tables, TOML requires. port = 8080 double R written integer TOML reader expects; non-whole doubles written shortest digits read back exactly. list named lists, data frame, becomes array tables. output every platform, reads back: NA NULL TOML form, refused unless na = "omit". Arrays past width characters written one element per line, inline = n writes small flat tables inline.
code: cfg <- list(   title = "Example",   port = 8080,   ratio = 0.75,   started = as.Date("2026-10-08"),   server = list(host = "localhost", tags = c("web", "api")),   users = list(list(name = "ana"), list(name = "bo")) ) cat(toml_emit(cfg)) #> title = "Example" #> port = 8080 #> ratio = 0.75 #> started = 2026-10-08 #>  #> [server] #> host = "localhost" #> tags = ["web", "api"] #>  #> [[users]] #> name = "ana" #>  #> [[users]] #> name = "bo" identical(toml_parse(toml_emit(cfg))$users, cfg$users) #> [1] TRUE

title: Usage guide
text: Many infrastructure tools configured TOML: Traefik, containerd, GitLab Runner, Telegraf, Netlify, Cloudflare’s wrangler.toml, Fly.io’s fly.toml. Reading one reading document, Traefik’s sample static configuration, pinned release: Writing TOML R pays : configuration generated data. Traefik dynamic configuration routes host set backends: ("websecure") keeps one-element array array, Traefik expects; list servers becomes array tables. Write Traefik watches files toml_write(dynamic, "dynamic.toml").
code: traefik <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/traefik/traefik/v3.7.14/traefik.sample.toml" static <- toml_read(traefik) names(static) #> [1] "global"      "entryPoints" "log"         "api"         "ping"        #> [6] "providers" static$entryPoints$websecure #> $address #> [1] ":443" backends <- c("http://10.0.0.1:8080", "http://10.0.0.2:8080") dynamic <- list(http = list(   routers = list(app = list(     rule = "Host(`app.example.com`)",     service = "app",     entryPoints = I("websecure"),     tls = list(certResolver = "letsencrypt")   )),   services = list(app = list(     loadBalancer = list(servers = lapply(backends, function(u) list(url = u)))   )) )) cat(toml_emit(dynamic)) #> [http.routers.app] #> rule = "Host(`app.example.com`)" #> service = "app" #> entryPoints = ["websecure"] #>  #> [http.routers.app.tls] #> certResolver = "letsencrypt" #>  #> [[http.services.app.loadBalancer.servers]] #> url = "http://10.0.0.1:8080" #>  #> [[http.services.app.loadBalancer.servers]] #> url = "http://10.0.0.2:8080"

what: Choose how one value is written
title: Usage guide
text: Markers change value written, never reads back : toml_inline() writes table inline, toml_literal() writes literal strings need escapes, toml_multiline() writes multi-line strings.
code: cat(toml_emit(list(   dependencies = list(     serde = toml_inline(list(version = "1.0", features = "derive")),     rand = "0.8"   ),   pattern = toml_literal("^\\d+\\.\\d+$"),   motd = toml_multiline("Welcome!") ))) #> pattern = '^\d+\.\d+$' #> motd = """ #> Welcome!""" #>  #> [dependencies] #> serde = { version = "1.0", features = "derive" } #> rand = "0.8"

what: Point at a value in the document
title: Usage guide
text: positions = TRUE records every key array element defined, check configuration can say problem : path column uses syntax select.
code:
cfg <- toml_parse("[server]
host = 'localhost'
port = 99999
", positions = TRUE) pos <- attr(cfg, "toml_positions") pos #>          path    type line column offset #> 1      server   table    1      2      1 #> 2 server.host  string    2      1      9 #> 3 server.port integer    3      1     28 at <- pos[pos$path == "server.port", ] sprintf("server.port (line %d, column %d) must be at most 65535", at$line, at$column) #> [1] "server.port (line 3, column 1) must be at most 65535"

title: Usage guide
text: toml_validate() runs whole check without building R value. returns TRUE FALSE, error = TRUE raises reason:
code:
toml_validate("a = 1
b = 2") #> [1] TRUE toml_validate("a = 1
a = 2") #> [1] FALSE try(toml_validate("a = 1
a = 2", error = TRUE)) #> Error : TOML parse error at line 2, column 1: key defined twice

title: Usage guide
text: Every error class, can caught kind. Parse errors carry line, column, byte offset kind fault: inherit zutoml_error. See ?"zutoml-conditions".
code:
err <- tryCatch(toml_parse("[t]
x = 1
[t]
"), zutoml_parse_error = function(e) e) c(err$kind, err$line, err$column) #> [1] "table_redefined" "3"               "2"

title: Usage guide
text: Four limits bound document can make zutoml , checked R value built:
code: try(toml_parse(paste0("a = ", strrep("[", 200)), max_depth = 64)) #> Error : TOML limit reached at line 1, column 69: the document nests deeper than max_depth = 64

title: Usage guide
text: zutoml reads TOML 1.1.0 default, adds \e \xHH escapes, times without seconds, newlines trailing commas inline tables. version = "1.0.0" reads strictly. emitter always writes text TOML 1.0.0 readers accept.
code: toml_parse("t = 07:30")$t #> [1] "07:30:00" try(toml_parse("t = 07:30", version = "1.0.0")) #> Error : TOML parse error at line 1, column 5: not a valid TOML date or time

code: config <- list(   title = "My service",   port = 8080,   debug = FALSE,   started = as.Date("2026-10-08"),   database = list(host = "localhost", ports = c(5432L, 5433L)),   servers = list(     list(name = "alpha", ip = "10.0.0.1"),     list(name = "beta", ip = "10.0.0.2")   ) ) cat(toml_emit(config)) #> title = "My service" #> port = 8080 #> debug = false #> started = 2026-10-08 #>  #> [database] #> host = "localhost" #> ports = [5432, 5433] #>  #> [[servers]] #> name = "alpha" #> ip = "10.0.0.1" #>  #> [[servers]] #> name = "beta" #> ip = "10.0.0.2" identical(toml_parse(toml_emit(config))$servers, config$servers) #> [1] TRUE cat(toml_emit(list(dependencies = list(   serde = toml_inline(list(version = "1.0", features = "derive")),   rand = "0.8" )))) #> [dependencies] #> serde = { version = "1.0", features = "derive" } #> rand = "0.8"

title: Read and Write TOML Documents
text: zutoml reads TOML documents ordinary R values writes R values TOML. parser writer written C, system library runtime dependencies. pass every case toml-test conformance suite, TOML 1.0.0 1.1.0. Types come document. 2024-01-01 Date; "2024-01-01" string. zutoml never guesses string’s content. Strict. invalid document refused, line column fault condition class can catch. Size, depth, item string limits bound untrusted input. Deterministic output. R value gives bytes every platform, text reads back.

title: Parse a TOML document — toml_parse
text: Reads TOML document ordinary R values: table becomes named list keys document order, array vector list, value R type . Types come document's syntax: "2024-01-01" stays string 2024-01-01 becomes Date. whole document checked, toml_validate(), R value built.

title: Parse a TOML document — toml_parse
code: toml_parse(   x,   select = NULL,   version = c("1.1.0", "1.0.0"),   simplify = c("preserve", "none"),   data_frame = FALSE,   big_integers = c("bigint", "double", "error"),   datetimes = c("convert", "keep"),   local_time = c("character", "difftime"),   positions = FALSE,   max_size = 64 * 1024^2,   max_depth = 128L,   max_items = 1e+06,   max_string = 2^31 - 1 )

title: Parse a TOML document — toml_parse
text: x TOML document: single string, raw vector UTF-8 bytes. select NULL (default) returns whole document. path returns value : string TOML key syntax, positions table writes ("tool.poetry"; '".b".c' key dot; "products[2].name" arrays, counting 1), vector two keys taken (c("tool", "poetry")). whole document still read checked, since TOML lets table added anywhere , selected part becomes R values. path document raises zutoml_missing_key, path found, part path exist. version TOML version read: "1.1.0" (default) "1.0.0", refuses forms 1.1.0 added (\e \xHH escapes, times without seconds, newlines trailing comma inline tables). simplify "preserve" (default) turns arrays whose elements share type vectors; "none" makes every array list. data_frame TRUE, array whose elements tables becomes data frame: one row per table, columns first-seen key order, missing keys NA. Columns whose values share type lists. getOption("zutoml.max_df_cells", 1e7) cells raises zutoml_limit_error, since rows share keys make frame quadratic size. big_integers integers beyond 2^53, double hold exactly: "bigint" (default) returns toml_bigint() vector exact decimal text; "double" nearest double; "error" raises zutoml_unrepresentable. datetimes "convert" (default) returns POSIXct Date; "keep" returns date-times text. local_time "character" (default) returns local time text; "difftime" seconds since midnight. positions TRUE, result carries attribute "toml_positions": data frame one row per key array element, order parsed value, giving path TOML key syntax (servers[2].ip, keys quoted TOML needs , array elements numbered 1), type ("table", "inline_table", "array_of_tables", "array", "string", "integer", "float", "bool", "datetime", "datetime-local", "date-local" "time-local"), line, column (1-based, characters) byte offset (0-based) defined: key's position keyed value, [[header]] table array tables. Code checks configuration can say value wrong. max_size largest document accepted, bytes, Inf. max_depth deepest nesting tables arrays, counting ; 1023. max_items keys plus array elements, Inf. max_string longest string key, decoded bytes, Inf.

title: Parse a TOML document — toml_parse
text: named list, one element per top-level key; select, value path.

title: Parse a TOML document — toml_parse
text: array becomes vector elements strings, booleans, numbers, dates, date-times one kind. Numbers widen: integers floats give double vector. Booleans never join numbers. empty array logical(0). one-element array becomes vector marked (), writing back gives array . Anything else list. simplify = "none" makes every array list. datetimes = "keep", date-times returned RFC 3339 text instead ("1979-05-27T07:32:00Z", zero offset written Z, fraction 0, 3, 6 9 digits). Fractions past nanoseconds truncated, TOML requires; POSIXct holds microseconds. Valid TOML R hold raises zutoml_unrepresentable: string key containing U+0000, float beyond range double, integer beyond 2^53 big_integers = "error".

title: Parse a TOML document — toml_parse
code: doc <- ' title = "TOML Example" ports = [8000, 8001, 8002]  [owner] name = "Tom Preston-Werner" dob = 1979-05-27T07:32:00-08:00  [[products]] name = "Hammer" sku = 738594937  [[products]] name = "Nail" sku = 284758393 color = "gray" ' x <- toml_parse(doc) x$owner$dob #> [1] "1979-05-27 15:32:00 UTC" x$ports #> [1] 8000 8001 8002  toml_parse(doc, data_frame = TRUE)$products #>     name       sku color #> 1 Hammer 738594937  <NA> #> 2   Nail 284758393  gray  # Only part of it: toml_parse(doc, select = "owner") #> $name #> [1] "Tom Preston-Werner" #>  #> $dob #> [1] "1979-05-27 15:32:00 UTC" #>  toml_parse(doc, select = "products[2].color") #> [1] "gray"  # Where each value is, for messages about the document: pos <- attr(toml_parse(doc, positions = TRUE), "toml_positions") pos[pos$path == "owner.dob", ] #>        path     type line column offset #> 8 owner.dob datetime    7      1     88

title: Conditions raised by zutoml — zutoml-conditions
text: Every error zutoml raises carries condition class, can caught kind rather matching message, may change. Every class inherits zutoml_error.

title: Conditions raised by zutoml — zutoml-conditions
text: zutoml_invalid_argument argument unusable, value written TOML given, list partial names string valid UTF-8. Carries arg, argument fault. zutoml_parse_error document TOML. Carries line column (1-based, characters), offset (0-based, bytes) kind, name rule broken, "bad_escape" "table_redefined". zutoml_unrepresentable document valid TOML holds value R : string containing U+0000, string longer R string, integer beyond 2^53 big_integers = "error". zutoml_unsupported_type R value TOML form, function, raw vector matrix. Carries path, key path value, .b[3].c. zutoml_na_error NA NULL value na = "error". Carries path. zutoml_limit_error limit reached. subclasses zutoml_size_limit, zutoml_depth_limit, zutoml_item_limit zutoml_string_limit name one. Carries limit, argument's name, "max_depth", limit_value. zutoml_io_error file, URL connection opened, read written. zutoml_missing_key toml_parse()'s select names path document . Carries path, path asked , found, part exists.

title: Conditions raised by zutoml — zutoml-conditions
code: tryCatch(   stop(structure(     class = c("zutoml_parse_error", "zutoml_error", "error", "condition"),     list(message = "TOML parse error", call = NULL)   )),   zutoml_error = function(e) class(e)[1] ) #> [1] "zutoml_parse_error"

title: zutoml 0.1.0
text: Initial CRAN submission. toml_read() reads TOML document file, URL connection, never holding max_size + 1 bytes. URL file opened zutoml_io_error naming cause (HTTP status '404 Found'), stray warning. toml_parse() reads TOML document ordinary R values: tables named lists document order, arrays vectors elements share type, date-times POSIXct Date, integers beyond 2^53 toml_bigint(). data_frame = TRUE turns arrays tables data frames. toml_emit() toml_write() write named list TOML: deterministic text, tables [headers], lists tables data frames arrays tables, errors name key path value fault. toml_parse(select = "tool.poetry"), toml_read(), returns value path, building R values rest document; path document raises zutoml_missing_key. toml_parse(positions = TRUE) records every key array element defined (path, type, line, column, offset), code checks configuration can point value fault. toml_inline(), toml_literal() toml_multiline() mark one value written toml_emit(). toml_validate() checks document valid TOML, within size, depth, item string limits, error = TRUE says (line, column, offset kind classed condition). zutoml_info() reports versions zutoml built toml-test suite passes. Every case toml-test suite passes, TOML 1.0.0 1.1.0, directions. TOML 1.1.0 read default; version = "1.0.0" reads strictly; emitter always writes TOML 1.0.0. vignette, vignette("zutoml"), reads pyproject.toml Cargo.toml writes configuration.
